note: a wrong name hanged, the culprit hidden

24.label: Beadle Hobson
24.desc: A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked. Slot them into a verb to help. Steady: Working beside them, you do not tire.

25.label: Informer: Two-Coats
25.desc: Bartel Barker, known in the taverns as Two-Coats. Works The Market. Meet them on the Ward with Coin for a word.

72.desc: From Burglary at Stromer's Pawnshop: three strokes cut where the crime began. A detail that belongs to no case. The same shape keeps turning up. Three of these, together in Rest, might show you the hand that draws it.

84.label: Beadle Kuiper
84.desc: A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked. Slot them into a verb to help. Thorough: Finds one more thing at every scene.

105.label: Confessor Tanner
105.desc: A priest without a parish. Sits. Listens. People tell him things they have never told God. Slot them into a verb to help. Patient: Study and the Watch take a fifth less time.

129.label: The Market
129.desc: Stalls, the weigh-house, pawnbrokers and cutpurses. The pillory stands in the square, and your Watch-house at its edge.

139.label: False Coin in the Cattle Market
139.desc: The Emperor's face has been getting smaller in the Cattle Market since the new coinage: every coin in the quarter a hair short. Somebody is shaving the edges and melting the harvest. In a locked drawer, a ledger in weights, not sums. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name. (The Market)

142.label: The Stews
142.desc: Taverns, bathhouses, dice-rooms and the spinning-house across the river. The people who own them own more than that.

147.label: The Scene Drawn
147.desc: Forty leaves of the Cattle Market in charcoal, numbered and dated. The room as it was.

149.label: Letter: Confessor
149.desc: A priest without a parish. Sits. Listens. People tell him things they have never told God. Costs 3 Coin.

161.label: The Light Scale
161.desc: every coin in the quarter a hair short. The Muhtasib tests weights on market day; this one was tested and passed, which means somebody was paid.

165.label: The Beggar's Word
165.desc: She stood where everyone passes, and nobody looks at a beggar. She looked at them.

169.label: Petition: Physician's Case
169.desc: Lancets, a silver needle, dried herbs in paper twists. Needed for blood and poison, sharpens anything of the body, and finds more of it at a scene. Costs 5 Coin.

170.label: Petition: Strongroom
170.desc: Tokens and raw proof keep twice as long behind an iron door. Costs 6 Coin.

182.label: Partial: The Mould Read
182.desc: Without the Vinegar and Umbrella, you only get part of it. Vinegar brings up the hand that pressed the plaster: a thumb, and a missing nail.

188.label: Protection in the Bakker Arcade
188.desc: Stallholders around the Bakker Arcade have been paying for "protection" every market day, collected by a boy who takes the purses. Kit Kempe refused, and lost their awning. Somewhere there is a receipt book. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name. (The Stews) The Guilds want the culprit shamed in the square or fined, and a brother of the guild not hanged.

189.label: Ned Chandler
189.desc: Ned Chandler, a sergeant of the Watch. Plays at dice every night in a cellar in the Stews. (Accused in: Protection in the Bakker Arcade)

190.label: Rumour from Two-Coats
190.desc: Two-Coats heard something about False Coin in the Cattle Market: "They smelled of pipe smoke. Cheap stuff, the Dutch kind."

191.label: Pipe Ash on the Sill
191.desc: A knocked-out bowl of ash on the windowsill, still sour. Someone waited here a long while, smoking.

192.label: Prime Suspect: Griet Sattler
192.desc: Griet Sattler, a tavern-keeper. Smokes a clay pipe of cheap Dutch tobacco, one bowl after another. (Accused in: False Coin in the Cattle Market)

193.label: Petition: The Hole
193.desc: A cell under the Watch-house with a table and one candle. Questioning is faster and draws out more Word. Costs 8 Coin.

194.label: Petition: The Apothecary's Key
194.desc: A key to the apothecary's back room and his patience. Needed for ledgers, letters and anything under the glass, and lets you take a token back to the bench once for more. Costs 5 Coin.

195.label: Petition: The Rolls
195.desc: The court's old books, shelved and indexed. Unanswered cases can be opened again in Study. Costs 8 Coin.

196.label: Petition: The Thief-takers' Office
196.desc: A room let to men who know every fence in the city. Put a Case in Attend with 2 Coin and they get the goods back for a cut, without a trial. Some of what they bring back is a frame. Costs 6 Coin.

197.label: Letter: Apothecary's Boy
197.desc: Talks to jars more than people. Knows the taste of every powder in the shop and which ones he should not have tasted. Costs 3 Coin.

201.label: Partial: The Clippings Assayed
201.desc: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Good silver, from the new coinage, and the same shears' bite on every edge.

203.label: Beadle Barker
203.desc: A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked. Slot them into a verb to help. Known: Doors open for them. A canvass turns up one more person.

208.label: Rumour from Two-Coats
208.desc: Two-Coats heard something about Protection in the Bakker Arcade: "They were rolling a die over their knuckles."

209.label: Witness: Matthes Vos
209.desc: Matthes Vos, the Mintmaster's assayer. Was at their casement and saw somebody near the Cattle Market, and has heard there is a reward. (Witness in: False Coin in the Cattle Market)

data.who: a market-woman who was paid in it

210.label: Witness: Griet Kessler
210.desc: Griet Kessler, a market-woman who was paid in it. Heard something near the Cattle Market, and is fond of somebody in the case. (Witness in: False Coin in the Cattle Market)

211.label: The Scene Drawn
211.desc: Forty leaves of the Bakker Arcade in charcoal, numbered and dated. The room as it was.

212.label: Motive: Ned Chandler
212.desc: The sergeant's round is exactly the streets being squeezed.

214.label: Warning: Protection
214.desc: Two-Coats says something is going to happen in The Market: protection. Keep this on the table. When the case comes in you will be ahead of it.

215.label: The Collectors
215.desc: a boy who takes the purses. Everybody has seen them. Nobody has seen them.

216.label: The Victim's Account
216.desc: Kit Kempe tells you everything, hands shaking, and begs you not to write their name down.

218.label: Barbel Kuiper
218.desc: Barbel Kuiper, the landlord of the arcade. Wears a pilgrim's cockle-shell on a greasy hat. (Accused in: Protection in the Bakker Arcade)

journal.title: Fever
journal.text: You read the same deposition four times and cannot say what is in it. The room tilts when you stand.

journal.title: Week 11
journal.text: You cannot pay your lodging. The landlord puts your chest in the lane at prime. You sleep in the Watch-house, on the bench. The Council elects next week. Your patron's seat is contested. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 4 Coin in hand.
parts: You cannot pay your lodging. The landlord puts your chest in the lane at prime. You sleep in the Watch-house, on the bench.
The Council elects next week. Your patron's seat is contested.
The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: The Council Elects
journal.text: Your patron's seat is contested. The other side has been counting the favours he did you. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Means and Moment
journal.text: Who wanted it, and who could have done it. When you lay the reason beside the chance, only one face fits both. It was Griet Sattler, a tavern-keeper. It has to be.

journal.title: Hunger
journal.text: You cannot remember your last hot meal. Your hands have started to shake on the stairs. Deal with it in Rest before the clock runs out.

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: A stallholder shakes your hand. A boy spits at your boots. An ordinary round. Alone in the lane, and it wore you out.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at the Bakker Arcade. You find: The Collectors · The Victim's Account · The Round. The first name in the casebook: Barbel Kuiper. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: A Warning
journal.text: "Protection," says Two-Coats, "in The Market. Soon. Don't ask me how I know."

journal.title: A Reason
journal.text: You let Ned Chandler talk about Kit Kempe. Their voice changes when they do. The sergeant's round is exactly the streets being squeezed. The silence held, and it wore you down to break it.

journal.title: Drawn
journal.text: You fill a sketch-book with the Bakker Arcade before anyone can tidy it. One thing you found there will keep now.

journal.title: Door to Door
journal.text: Around the Cattle Market people are frightened, and frightened people talk. You come away with: Witness: Matthes Vos; Witness: Griet Kessler. One door stayed shut, and the street talked less for it.

journal.title: A Word from Two-Coats
journal.text: A folded paper pushed under the Watch-house door, about Protection in the Bakker Arcade. Two-Coats does not sign things.

journal.title: Week 10
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 3. The Council's stipend: 2 Coin. The ledger: 1 conviction; 2 open; 3 Coin in hand. The Council's favour rises.
parts: The ledger: 1 conviction; 2 open; 3 Coin in hand.

journal.title: The Rival Exposed
journal.text: A token they spoiled, and the lane where their people were seen. The Council reads the file in silence and sends the Harbourmaster's Examiner back to the Customs House. Your name is spoken in the chamber, warmly for once. In the examiner's desk, a leaf from the Customs House: what the Harbourmaster paid, and for what.

journal.title: Delivered: Vinegar and Umbrella
journal.text: It arrives by carrier in a crate with the wrong name on it. It works perfectly.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Hans Barker takes the oath at the Watch-house door. A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Good silver, from the new coinage, and the same shears' bite on every edge.

journal.title: Promoted: Sworn Examiner
journal.text: You swear the oath in the Council chamber with your hand on the Carolina, and the clerk writes your name under the last Examiner's, which has a line through it. You are now Sworn Examiner. A magistrate will seal a Writ for you (an Accused with cause, in Explore), and the Council sends you more. The Council will send you up to 3 cases at once, and pay 2 a week.

journal.title: The Office Teaches
journal.text: New work, new lessons: The Writ's Weight. The Health, Wit and Instinct cards say how each is earned.

journal.title: The Watch Takes the Round
journal.text: You send a watchman out in your place and sit down for the first time since prime.

journal.title: Cleared: Magdalena Schmidt
journal.text: You try Magdalena Schmidt's story. It holds: a carrier's chit stamped two days' ride away. Strike one name from the casebook.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over the Cattle Market. You find: Pipe Ash on the Sill. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Griet Sattler. The counting-room stayed locked, and its books with it.

journal.title: A Word from Two-Coats
journal.text: A folded paper pushed under the Watch-house door, about False Coin in the Cattle Market. Two-Coats does not sign things.

journal.title: A Commission from The Guilds: Protection in the Bakker Arcade
journal.text: Stallholders around the Bakker Arcade have been paying for "protection" every market day, collected by a boy who takes the purses. Kit Kempe refused, and lost their awning. Somewhere there is a receipt book. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name. The Guilds want the culprit shamed in the square or fined, and a brother of the guild not hanged.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A cup of small beer at the Watch-house door, and the street comes back into focus.

journal.title: The Rope: Michel Seiler
journal.text: The staff is broken. Michel Seiler hangs on the Ravenstone before the whole city, and the ballad-sellers have the verses printed by nones. The crowd goes home satisfied.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without the Vinegar and Umbrella, you only get part of it. Vinegar brings up the hand that pressed the plaster: a thumb, and a missing nail. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: Your Health is more than it was.
journal.text: A gentleman on the Hill, retired from a regiment nobody names, has watched you walk the hard round past his window three nights running. You are more than you were.

journal.title: Guilty: Michel Seiler
journal.text: The sworn men are out for the length of a Paternoster. Michel Seiler is convicted of Burglary at the Tucher House, and the sergeants take them down to the Hole to wait for the sentence. The Council's thanks, with a purse attached.

journal.title: Condemned: Michel Seiler
journal.text: Michel Seiler goes down to the Hole to wait. The ladder is on your desk: Pardon, A Fine, Pillory, Banished, Branded, The Rope. The Council will follow your word, or its custom. Pleas arrive with the morning: A Family's Plea.

journal.title: The Petitions
journal.text: A clerk brings the forms the Council will now hear from you: instruments, rooms, a key. Each Petition in Attend with its price in Coin.

journal.title: Week 9
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. Piet Wieland spoiled a token of yours. A letter of service lands on your desk: Beadle. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 4 Coin in hand.
parts: Piet Wieland spoiled a token of yours.
A letter of service lands on your desk: Beadle.
The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: A Scene Spoiled
journal.text: Somebody has been at The Beggar's Word before you could use it: moved, wiped, muddled. Piet Wieland's people were seen in the lane.

journal.title: The Beggar at the Door: Give her a Coin
journal.text: The child gets bread. She tells you who came and went, and the clerks get a story about you. (The Crowd and Dread ease; her word on the case)

journal.title: The Beggar at the Door
journal.text: A woman with a child on her hip has been at the Watch-house door since prime. She does not ask for anything. She just stands there, where the Council's clerks can see her, and she has seen everyone who passed. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at the Cattle Market. You find: The Light Scale · A Plaster Mould · A ledger in weights, not sums. The first name in the casebook: Magdalena Schmidt.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: A bed at the Swan, a fire in the room and a door that locks. You sleep like a councillor.

journal.title: Your Wit is more than it was.
journal.text: The sergeant has seen every examiner burn out the same way. You are more than you were.

journal.title: Interrupted
journal.text: Burglary at the Tucher House went to the Court while you were at it.

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: You spend six hours on your feet in the rain outside the bear-garden. Your feet ache all the way up to your skull. Alone in the lane, and it wore you out.

journal.title: An Insight: The Fencing-master
journal.text: A gentleman on the Hill, retired from a regiment nobody names, has watched you walk the hard round past his window three nights running. He offers to teach you the rapier. It is not really about the rapier. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: Interrupted
journal.text: Burglary at the Tucher House went to the Court while you were at it.

journal.title: A Hot Dinner
journal.text: Mutton, bread, small beer, and a second helping. Your hands stop shaking somewhere around the pudding.

journal.title: Taken: Michel Seiler
journal.text: The sergeants take them at the city gate, one foot on the carrier's wagon. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: Your Instinct is more than it was.
journal.text: An informer trusts you now, which in this city is rarer than gold. You are more than you were.

journal.title: A Warning
journal.text: "Protection," says Two-Coats, "in The Stews. Soon. Don't ask me how I know."

journal.title: Cleared: Lienhard Tanner
journal.text: Lienhard Tanner has an answer, and it is a good one: a night in the Hole for drunkenness. They are cleared.

journal.title: Hunger
journal.text: You cannot remember your last hot meal. Your hands have started to shake on the stairs. Deal with it in Rest before the clock runs out.

journal.title: Week 8
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. Piet Wieland spoiled a token of yours. A letter of service lands on your desk: Confessor. The ledger: 1 conviction; 2 open; 6 Coin in hand. The Council's favour falls.
parts: Piet Wieland spoiled a token of yours.
A letter of service lands on your desk: Confessor.
The ledger: 1 conviction; 2 open; 6 Coin in hand.

journal.title: A Scene Spoiled
journal.text: Somebody has been at Partial: The Wards Read before you could use it: moved, wiped, muddled. Piet Wieland's people were seen in the lane.

journal.title: The Watch Takes the Round
journal.text: You send a watchman out in your place and sit down for the first time since prime.

journal.title: Drawn
journal.text: You fill a sketch-book with the Cattle Market before anyone can tidy it. Whatever you find there next will be on record.

journal.title: The Rope: Regina Bader
journal.text: The staff is broken. Regina Bader hangs on the Ravenstone before the whole city, and the ballad-sellers have the verses printed by nones. The crowd goes home satisfied.

journal.title: Corroborated Account
journal.text: The body of the thing and the words of the witnesses finally agree. They point the same way. It was Michel Seiler, the owner's partner in trade. It has to be.

journal.title: An Insight: The Sergeant's Patience
journal.text: The sergeant has seen every examiner burn out the same way. He shows you how he sits down between things: how he lets a case go for the length of a pipe, and comes back to it. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: New Ground: The Stews
journal.text: Your feet take you somewhere new. Taverns, bathhouses, dice-rooms and the spinning-house across the river. The people who own them own more than that. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: The Council Takes Notice
journal.text: A letter on heavy paper under the city's seal: the Council will see you about the office of Sworn Examiner. Attend on them, in a clean collar.

journal.title: New Case: False Coin in the Cattle Market
journal.text: The Emperor's face has been getting smaller in the Cattle Market since the new coinage: every coin in the quarter a hair short. Somebody is shaving the edges and melting the harvest. In a locked drawer, a ledger in weights, not sums. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name.

journal.title: Guilty: Regina Bader
journal.text: The sworn men are out for the length of a Paternoster. Regina Bader is convicted of Protection in Molenaar Lane, and the sergeants take them down to the Hole to wait for the sentence. A Council family in the dock. The Hill will not forgive it, and the Stews will not forget it. The Watch-house fee is paid to the coin, and not a penny over.

journal.title: Condemned: Regina Bader
journal.text: Regina Bader goes down to the Hole to wait. The ladder is on your desk: Pardon, Pillory, Banished, Branded, The Rope. The Council will follow your word, or its custom.

journal.title: The Market
journal.text: The stallholders know your face now. The Quarter is yours to walk: put it in Explore with Health for a round, or with a case to look for its people there.

journal.title: A Warning
journal.text: "Coining," says Two-Coats, "in The Market. Soon. Don't ask me how I know."

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: The round hears things: a word about Burglary at the Tucher House.

journal.title: A Weakness Found
journal.text: Two hours of polite questions, and a name they did not want spoken: a moneylender, a widow, a file of their own. They have been asking about Burglary at the Tucher House. Now catch them at it: bring what they spoiled, a witness they paid or a case they took to Question, or answer their case in the Blood Court first.

journal.title: A Word
journal.text: Two-Coats counts the coin twice before talking. It is worth it. They know something about Burglary at the Tucher House.

journal.title: An Insight: A Word in the Right Ear
journal.text: An informer trusts you now, which in this city is rarer than gold. They tell you which tapster to buy, and which to be seen buying. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over the Tucher House. You find: A Left-Handed Stroke · A Key, Not a Crow. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Michel Seiler.

journal.title: Taken: Regina Bader
journal.text: The sergeants take them at their shop, in front of everyone. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: Week 7
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The Harbourmaster has sent an examiner of his own. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 5 Coin in hand.
parts: The Harbourmaster has sent an examiner of his own.
The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 5 Coin in hand.

journal.title: The Harbourmaster's Examiner
journal.text: Piet Wieland has the Harbourmaster's letter and a desk in the Customs House. The Harbourmaster wants the Council to see it has a choice. They will work your cases from the other side: close them first, spoil your scenes, pay your witnesses to forget. Question them, buy them, frighten them, or shadow them; find their weakness twice and the Council sends them home.

journal.title: The Watch Takes the Round
journal.text: You send a watchman out in your place and sit down for the first time since prime.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: The round hears things: a word about Burglary at the Tucher House.

journal.title: The Pawnbroker's Book: Buy the page
journal.text: A page in a bad hand, with a name on it that you were going to have to find the hard way. (A token that names a name)

journal.title: The Pawnbroker's Book
journal.text: A pawnbroker keeps a book of everything that came through his door this week, and who brought it. Something from your case is in it. He would part with the page. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Wax in the keyhole takes the wards: a key cut new from a borrowed one, by a locksmith who did not ask. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: A Word from Two-Coats
journal.text: A folded paper pushed under the Watch-house door, about Burglary at the Tucher House. Two-Coats does not sign things.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: A bed at the Swan, a fire in the room and a door that locks. You sleep like a councillor.

journal.title: Corroborated Account
journal.text: The body of the thing and the words of the witnesses finally agree. They point the same way. It was Regina Bader, a bravo of the Stews. It has to be.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle. Nothing at the Tucher House was forced. They came in by the front door, with a key, and shut it again behind them. You come away with The Lock Unmarked, The Inventory. A name for the casebook: Endres Bicker. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: Cleared: Pieter Haller
journal.text: You try Pieter Haller's story. It holds: a wedding, and forty guests who remember the dancing. Strike one name from the casebook.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Lienhard Tanner takes the oath at the Watch-house door. A priest without a parish. Sits. Listens. People tell him things they have never told God.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without the Vinegar and Umbrella, you only get part of it. The blackmailer's own hand, on the thing they were most careful about. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: Week 6
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. A letter of service lands on your desk: Confessor. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 10 Coin in hand. The Bishop's favour falls.
parts: A letter of service lands on your desk: Confessor.
The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 10 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Drawn
journal.text: You fill a sketch-book with the Tucher House before anyone can tidy it. Two things you found there will keep now.

journal.title: Entered
journal.text: Four hours with the quill. By the end, even the parts that were not quite by the Carolina read as if they were.

journal.title: A Word from Two-Coats
journal.text: A folded paper pushed under the Watch-house door, about Burglary at the Tucher House. Two-Coats does not sign things.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Molenaar Lane. You find: A copy of a letter that should not exist · The Slashed Awning.  The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Entered
journal.text: Four hours with the quill. By the end, even the parts that were not quite by the Carolina read as if they were.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Your Wit is more than it was.
journal.text: Full proof before the Blood Court, and the judge asked who taught you. You are more than you were.

journal.title: A Room at the Swan: Take the room
journal.text: You sleep like the dead and wake like the living. (Weariness lifts)

journal.title: A Room at the Swan
journal.text: The landlord of the Swan, who owes the Watch a kindness, offers a room with a fire and a door that locks. One night. Tonight. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: The Confessor: Ask him to point
journal.text: He does not say a word. He looks, once, at a door, and goes back inside to pray for both of you. (A token that names a name; the Bishop frowns)

journal.title: The Confessor
journal.text: A priest of the parish asks for a word. Someone told him something under the seal, and it is eating him. He will not break the seal. He might point. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at Molenaar Lane. You find: The Price · A Curved Scratch. The first name in the casebook: Pieter Haller. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Cleared: Ottilie Weber
journal.text: You try Ottilie Weber's story. It holds: a bed in the Abbey hospital. Strike one name from the casebook.

journal.title: The Rope: Endres Claesz
journal.text: The staff is broken. Endres Claesz hangs on the Ravenstone before the whole city, and the ballad-sellers have the verses printed by nones. The crowd goes home satisfied. The Bishop's chaplain will remember that you were asked.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Caspar Kuiper takes the oath at the Watch-house door. A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked.

journal.title: Week 5
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. A letter of service lands on your desk: Beadle. The ledger: 1 conviction; 2 open; 11 Coin in hand.
parts: A letter of service lands on your desk: Beadle.
The ledger: 1 conviction; 2 open; 11 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Guilty: Endres Claesz
journal.text: The sworn men are out for the length of a Paternoster. Endres Claesz is convicted of Burglary at Stromer's Pawnshop, and the sergeants take them down to the Hole to wait for the sentence. The Council's thanks, with a purse attached. At the court door Margery Sattler presses a coin into your hand and will not take it back. An honest fee. But one detail belongs to no one in the case: a small mason's mark, three strokes, cut where the crime began. You have seen it before.

journal.title: Condemned: Endres Claesz
journal.text: Endres Claesz goes down to the Hole to wait. The ladder is on your desk: Pardon, A Fine, Pillory, Banished, Branded, The Rope. The Council will follow your word, or its custom. Pleas arrive with the morning: The Bishop's Plea, A Family's Plea.

journal.title: An Insight: The Old Examiner's Method
journal.text: Full proof before the Blood Court, and the judge asked who taught you. Nobody did. But in the drawer of your desk is a leaf in the last examiner's hand, and reading it now, you understand it. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: A Word from Two-Coats
journal.text: A folded paper pushed under the Watch-house door, about Burglary at the Tucher House. Two-Coats does not sign things.

journal.title: A Hot Dinner
journal.text: Mutton, bread, small beer, and a second helping. Your hands stop shaking somewhere around the pudding.

journal.title: Hunger
journal.text: You cannot remember your last hot meal. Your hands have started to shake on the stairs. Deal with it in Rest before the clock runs out.

journal.title: Pocketed
journal.text: Three weeks' stipend in worn silver. It sits in your coat like a stone. Somewhere, somebody writes your name in a ledger.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A cup of small beer at the Watch-house door, and the street comes back into focus.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Hans Hobson walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: New Case: Burglary at the Tucher House
journal.text: No broken glass at Neeltje Molenaar's. Whoever came in overnight used the front door, with a key, and left with three silver spoons and a ledger. A neighbour reports seeing the candle go on and off again, as if someone knew the house. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name.

journal.title: Drawn
journal.text: You fill a sketch-book with Molenaar Lane before anyone can tidy it. Whatever you find there next will be on record.

journal.title: Interrupted
journal.text: Burglary at Stromer's Pawnshop went to the Court while you were at it.

journal.title: Taken: Endres Claesz
journal.text: The sergeants take them at first light, on their doorstep. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: A bed at the Swan, a fire in the room and a door that locks. You sleep like a councillor.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A cup of small beer at the Watch-house door, and the street comes back into focus.

journal.title: Week 4
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. There is a purse on your desk. Nobody saw who left it. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 6 Coin in hand.
parts: There is a purse on your desk. Nobody saw who left it.
The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 6 Coin in hand.

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: A stallholder shakes your hand. A boy spits at your boots. An ordinary round. Alone in the lane, and it wore you out.

journal.title: The Watch Takes the Round
journal.text: You send a watchman out in your place and sit down for the first time since prime.

journal.title: A Warning
journal.text: "Burglary," says Two-Coats, "in Patricians' Hill. Soon. Don't ask me how I know."

journal.title: A Commission from The Council: Protection in Molenaar Lane
journal.text: Barbel Bakker has been paying since the letter, because of a copy of a letter that should not exist. What is wanted is silence about a name. They came to you because they cannot pay any more. The Council wants it answered within 21 days, and would take it kindly if Regina Bader, of a Council family, were not the name.

journal.title: Means and Moment
journal.text: Who wanted it, and who could have done it. When you lay the reason beside the chance, only one face fits both. It was Endres Claesz, a nephew of the house. It has to be.

journal.title: A Small Kindness
journal.text: You catch a cutpurse at the corner of the Market. The stallholder presses coin into your hand and will not take it back. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: A Deposition
journal.text: You sit. You listen. You let the silence do the work. Eventually the Tiler says: "They kept asking when the carrier's wagon left."

journal.title: Week 3
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 3 Coin in hand. The Council's favour rises.
parts: The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 3 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without the Vinegar and Umbrella, you only get part of it. Under vinegar and the red umbrella the hand comes up whole: a thumb with a scar across it. Good enough for the Court.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Stromer's Pawnshop. You find: The Second Key. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Endres Claesz. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: The round hears things: a word about Burglary at Stromer's Pawnshop.

journal.title: A Word from Two-Coats
journal.text: A folded paper pushed under the Watch-house door, about Burglary at Stromer's Pawnshop. Two-Coats does not sign things.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: A bed at the Swan, a fire in the room and a door that locks. You sleep like a councillor.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: You sit on the stair with your head in your hands until it stops. It stops.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Cheap leaf, sold at two shops in the city. Both keep a slate for regulars. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: The Clerk's Favour: Lose the file
journal.text: The Council owes you one, and knows you can be asked. A purse follows the clerk out. (Council favour +2; a Coin in thanks)

journal.title: The Clerk's Favour
journal.text: The Council's clerk lingers after delivering the stipend. A councillor's son was found where he should not have been, with people he should not have known. There is a file. It would be a kindness if there were not. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: You sit on the stair with your head in your hands until it stops. It stops.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Stromer's Pawnshop. You find: Pipe Ash in the Study · Marks on the Sill. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Kunz Pietersz.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A cup of small beer at the Watch-house door, and the street comes back into focus.

journal.title: Trouble at the Swan: Watch who leaves
journal.text: You let it burn out and watch the door. The potboy sees you watching, and sees a living in it. (An Informer at the Swan)

journal.title: Trouble at the Swan
journal.text: The round passes the Swan as two carters go through its window. The tapster is shouting your name. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Hans Hobson takes the oath at the Watch-house door. A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: A bed at the Swan, a fire in the room and a door that locks. You sleep like a councillor.

journal.title: Week 2
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 4 Coin in hand.
parts: The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Wax in the keyhole takes the wards: a key cut new from a borrowed one, by a locksmith who did not ask. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: A stallholder shakes your hand. A boy spits at your boots. An ordinary round.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle. Nothing at Stromer's Pawnshop was forced. They came in by the cellar hatch, and shut it again behind them. You come away with The Lock Unmarked, The Inventory. A name for the casebook: Regina Schmidt. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A cup of small beer at the Watch-house door, and the street comes back into focus.

journal.title: The Tiler's Word: A Coin for his trouble
journal.text: He saw a face, and he will say so again where it counts. (A Witness who saw it)

journal.title: The Tiler's Word
journal.text: A tiler was on his ladder across the lane when it happened, mending a roof that did not need mending. He says so to anyone with a coin, and now he is saying it to you. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Drawn
journal.text: You fill a sketch-book with Stromer's Pawnshop before anyone can tidy it. Whatever you find there next will be on record.

journal.title: Somebody's Casebook
journal.text: The drawer of your new desk still has the last examiner's quills in it, and a leaf torn from a casebook with one word underlined three times. You put it in your coat and open the first case.

journal.title: New Case: Burglary at Stromer's Pawnshop
journal.text: Margery Sattler is not sure when it happened: during the wedding downstairs. Only the cellar hatch was touched, and only the strongbox, opened rather than forced taken. A neighbour reports seeing a guest who left early. Somebody knew the house.

choice.title: The Council Elects
choice.text: Your patron's seat is contested. The other side has been counting the favours he did you.

options.label: Stand with him openly
options.text: You dine at his table the night before the count, where the chamber can see you.
options.gain: If he holds the seat, Council favour +2; if not, Suspicion for every favour

options.label: Keep your distance
options.text: You are busy at the Watch-house all week, and say so to anyone who asks.
options.gain: Favour halves; no Suspicion either way

options.label: Dine with the other side
options.text: The other side keeps a good table, and the Bishop's chaplain hears whose.
options.gain: Council favour +1 under the new man; Bishop -1
